subject: Trial capacity probe: proposed schedule, data intake, and success matrix
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@acmeai.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Trial capacity probe: proposed schedule, data intake, and success matrix

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet the ACME team. Per our discussion, the next step is a short capacity probe (3 phases) to validate production latency and cost at realistic burst patterns before we finalize the POC sizing. I captured the proposed deliverables below and a short data intake we need from your side.

High-level plan (proposed):
- Phase A (baseline): 1 hour sustained at expected steady RPS to validate p50/p95 under steady state.
- Phase B (burst simulation): two 60s bursts at 3x baseline, followed by a 5m cool-down to check KV cache behavior.
- Phase C (production-mix soak): 30 minutes with mixed prompt lengths (short + long generations) to validate tail latency and token costs.

Data we need from ACME to configure the probe: (please paste into attached probe-plan-template.csv)
1) Sustained RPS (typical steady): e.g., 30 RPS
2) Burst peak RPS and duration: e.g., 700 RPS for 45s, frequency (daily/weekly)
3) Concurrency: number of concurrent clients/sessions and whether bursts are correlated across tenants
4) Token length distribution: median and 90/99 percentiles for prompt tokens and generation tokens; max observed token length
5) Error tolerance & acceptance criteria: acceptable p95 latency, error rate, and cost guardrails
6) Test endpoints and any auth/test keys we should use

Preliminary acceptance criteria (we can iterate):
- p95 latency under 450ms for typical requests at baseline; p95 under 1s during peak bursts (depending on tradeoffs)
- Production error rate < 0.5% during probe windows
- No client-visible failures and successful KV cache reuse within burst windows

Proposed date for the capacity probe: week of Apr 27. Can you confirm availability for Apr 28 (engineering sync + test run)? I attached a blank probe-plan-template.csv — please fill and return.

If you want, we can run the Phase A baseline first and pause before burst simulation; will defer to your ops/cust requirements.

Next steps:
- Elena: paste numbers into the attached CSV and attach a small workload sample if available (acme-workload-sample.json)
- ACME infra: provide a test key for probe traffic and a contact for on-call during test runs
- Redwood: we will prepare a probe schedule and a success matrix; Lauren will own infra run, Sergio will coordinate customer comms.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Markus Klein
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
From: Elena Torres <elena@acmeai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial capacity probe: proposed schedule, data intake, and success matrix

Thanks Markus — good recap. Attached is a short workload sample and I pasted the key numbers inline below while our infra team fills the CSV: 

- Typical sustained RPS: 30 RPS (steady daytime traffic)
- Peak burst: ~700 RPS for ~45 seconds, typically occurs when our nightly batch finishes (daily)
- Concurrency: our front-end opens ~60 concurrent sessions; however not all generate requests at the same instant. Bursts are usually correlated across ~10% of customers during batch completion.
- Token distribution (rough): prompt tokens median 40, 90th 160, max observed 600. Generation tokens avg 220, 90th 550, rare max 1200 (long document generation).
- Acceptance criteria from ACME side: p95 < 450ms for typical short requests; for long generations we'd accept higher tail (p95 < 1.2s). Error rate must stay below 0.5%.

We attached acme-workload-sample.json (short set of 50 representative requests) — hopefully that helps with token sampling. Apr 28 works for an initial baseline run; please share a calendar invite.

Elena
Head of Platform, Acme AI
elena@acmeai.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@acmeai.com>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 11:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial capacity probe: proposed schedule, data intake, and success matrix

Appreciate the numbers — that helps a lot. A few clarifying questions before I finalize the probe schedule: 
1) Can you confirm how frequently the ~700 RPS bursts occur (every day at batch completion or more sporadic)? You mentioned daily but want to confirm whether there are week-over-week pattern differences.
2) For the long generations (rare max 1200 tokens) — are those single-request long outputs or chunked multi-request flows? If single requests, we'll treat them as heavy-tail cases in Phase C.
3) Do you have a staging/test key we should use for initial runs, and is there an infra contact for live troubleshooting?

Prelim sizing note (subject to probe): based on the sample and your bursts, our recommended starting config for the probe is a dedicated pool (reserved) sized to mimic production concurrency: 8 x A800 (logical) equivalents with model quantized to 4-bit for cost testing. We'll also tune batching target to prefer lower latency for short prompts (batch at ~32 tokens when possible) and allow larger batches during soak.

Proposed probe schedule (draft):
- Apr 28 10:00 - 10:30 UTC: Phase A baseline (steady 30 RPS)
- Apr 28 11:00 - 11:10 UTC: Phase B burst test (two 60s bursts at 700 RPS)
- Apr 28 11:30 - 12:00 UTC: Phase C soak (mixed traffic)

Success matrix (examples we will record): p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, token/sec, cost-per-token estimate, KV cache hit ratio, and ingestion/backpressure events. If any of these cross the thresholds we will stop and debrief.

I attached a short calendar stub (probe-schedule.ics) and will send a formal invite once we lock Rahul (your infra lead) in.

— Markus
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:00:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: ACME probe owners and runbook

Folks — looping you both in with the ACME numbers we received. Quick owner assignment: 
- Sergio: customer comms and scheduling (you own the call with Elena and Rahul)
- Lauren: infra run and metrics dashboard; run the probe from the dedicated pool and collect the success matrix metrics.
- Markus: lead the test plan and be on the call for debugging.

Checklist for the run:
- Confirm test key from ACME and verify auth (5 min)
- Warm KV cache with 5 minutes of sample traffic before Phase B
- Run Phase A and validate p50/p95; if p95 > 750ms we pause and adjust batching
- Execute Phase B burst; watch error rate and p99; abort if error rate > 1%
- Run Phase C soak and produce token-cost estimates

I'll post run artifacts to #sales-pocs/acme (Slack) and to the Drive folder in related_links. Lauren — can you create the dashboard with these widgets: real-time RPS, p50/p95/p99, token/sec, cost estimate, KV hit ratio, and infra GPU utilization?

Thanks — will update once they confirm the test key.

— Markus
From: Elena Torres <elena@acmeai.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rahul Singh <rahul@acmeai.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 12:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Trial capacity probe: proposed schedule, data intake, and success matrix

Thanks all — Rahul (cc'ed) is our infra lead and he'll provide a staging key by EOD today. Apr 28 window looks good. A couple of quick asks from our side:
- Can Redwood include a header in responses during the probe to indicate batching level and pool id (helps our tracing)?
- Please share the expected rate-limit headers you will emit so we can map them to our client backoff logic.

Rahul — I flagged Apr 28 10:00 UTC as tentative on our calendar; please confirm.

Best,
Elena
